function.mechanism: Conjugated carotenoid chromophore absorbs blue-violet light, producing yellow-orange coloration.
common_food_categories: EU-authorized food additive uses assessed by EFSA

adi.basis: EFSA ANS re-evaluation (2010) set ADI at 1 mg/kg bw/day from NOAEL 200 mg/kg bw/day with UF 200; 2012 statement refined exposure estimates but retained child high-consumer caveat.

efsa.key_finding: E161b remained in authorized-use context, but EFSA identified possible ADI exceedance for high-consuming children under some exposure scenarios.

fda.notes: Listed as Tagetes (Aztec marigold) meal and extract color additive exempt from certification, with use limited to chicken feed; no lutein/tagetes listing found in 21 CFR Part 184 GRAS scan.

adi.basis: At the 86th JECFA (2018), a group ADI of not specified was established for lutein from Tagetes erecta, lutein esters from Tagetes erecta, and synthetic zeaxanthin, superseding the 2004 group ADI of 0-2 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: EFSA exposure assessments identified potential ADI exceedance in high-consuming child subpopulations (toddlers/pre-school/school children) under some use scenarios.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA (2018) assigned a group ADI of not specified for lutein from Tagetes erecta and related carotenoids.
Cochrane review in preterm infants reported no adverse effects in included lutein/zeaxanthin studies.
Recent rodent toxicology report (PMID 41596229) described no treatment-related adverse effects in the tested preparation.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA child high-consumer exceedance concern persisted after exposure refinement, while most other groups were below ADI in refined scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory authorities continue to permit lutein under specified conditions, but EFSA repeatedly flagged child high-end exposure relative to ADI, which is a material caveat above a simple low-concern profile.
key_factors: EFSA ADI is numeric (1 mg/kg bw/day) with child high-consumer exceedance scenarios
JECFA 2018 group ADI is not specified
US CFR listing is a restricted approval context (chicken feed color additive)
Recent clinical/toxicology literature did not show strong adverse-event signals at studied doses
